g1-implement.title: Engine: add the report-only `basis` field (schema, render, attest guard)
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate: implement the new `basis` sibling field on Condition in scripts/checklist_engine.py per PLAN_ALTERNATIVES.md's design: (1) `render_human` (~line 2679-2749, inside the preconditions/postconditions loop) emits one indented sub-line `  basis: <locator_kind> <locator>` under an open condition ONLY when `c.get('basis')` is populated and `locator_kind != 'abstain'` -- populated-only, same convention as constraints/anchors/directives. (2) `attest()` (~line 3404-3472), inside the existing `chk is None` branch, gains a new guard: when the condition carries a populated, non-abstain `basis`, resolve its locator (`file`: check the path/glob exists under base_dir; `evidence_ref`: walk cl['tasks'][task_id] for cond_id, require it satisfied with non-null satisfied_by) BEFORE the unconditional accept, and ALWAYS attach a durable `basis-check` evidence item recording {locator_kind, locator, resolved: bool} regardless of outcome -- on failure this is report-only (attach the evidence, proceed, do not raise) since this is genuinely new attest code with no live precedent per decision:widening-live-refusal-report-only. Add a small pure dispatcher `_resolve_basis_locator(cl, base_dir, basis) -> str | None` (None = resolved). Do NOT implement `state_field` or `command` locator kinds (named untaken roads only). Write the red-proof FIRST against a throwaway fixture checklist (not the real shipped template, which g2 edits): a test demonstrating (a) a `check: null` condition with no `basis` attests exactly as before (unchanged legacy behavior), (b) a condition with a populated `file` basis whose target is missing still attests successfully (report-only) but records a `basis-check` evidence item with resolved: false, (c) the same with the target present records resolved: true, (d) `render_human` emits the basis sub-line only when populated. Validate as a fresh-process run (a standalone `python scripts/checklist_engine.py ...` CLI invocation or pytest) per the mission frame's dogfooding constraint -- do not rely on this run's own live MCP door as evidence. Document the field in docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Condition table and add a short new subsection describing the report-only guard and its promotion trigger (an Admiral audit of accumulated `basis-check` evidence across real runs). Dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer with the completed handoff via `python scripts/run_crew.py --backend cli --parent "$SPINE_SESSION" --work-id w2-basis --gate g1 --role implementer --model sonnet ...` per references/crew-dispatch.md. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT: attach it as `implementer-result` evidence with field name `status`, value copied verbatim lowercase from the result's Return status.
